t: ArduPilot: What ArduPilot Is: The Veteran Autopilot
title: ArduPilot: What ArduPilot Is: The Veteran Autopilot
description: ArduPilot is the longest-running open-source autopilot: one codebase, many vehicles — Copter for multicopters, Plane for fixed-wings, Rover for ground vehicles, Boat, Sub for underwater, even antennas and balloons. It speaks MAVLink natively, runs on Pixhawk and dozens of boards, and its feature depth (terrain following, precision landing, crop-sprayer support) reflects two decades of field use. Where PX4 is the modern rewrite, ArduPilot is the battle-tested elder — and many commercial vehicles fly it.

t: ArduPilot: Flight Modes Across Vehicle Types
title: ArduPilot: Flight Modes Across Vehicle Types
description: ArduPilot's modes span vehicles: Copter's Loiter, AltHold, Auto, RTL, and SmartRTL (retraces its path home); Plane's FBWA/FBWB stabilized modes, Auto, RTL, and soaring support; Rover's Manual, Auto, RTL. The mode vocabulary is the operator's contract with the machine — each mode documents what the vehicle decides and what the human decides. Learning a new vehicle type starts with its modes.

title: ArduPilot: EKF3 and Sensor Fusion
description: ArduPilot's EKF3 fuses IMU (often dual or triple), GPS (multi-constellation, multi-receiver), barometer, compass, optical flow, and rangefinders into the navigation solution, with per-sensor health and automatic source switching. The 'EKF lane switching' — jumping to a backup IMU when the primary degrades — is the kind of redundancy that saves aircraft. Compass calibration (the famous compass dance) and vibration management are the field rituals that make the filter happy.

title: ArduPilot: Lua Scripting: Autonomy Onboard
description: ArduPilot's Lua scripting runs user code on the flight controller itself: custom behaviors, sensor drivers, companion-lite logic — sandboxed, with bindings to vehicle state and MAVLink. Scripts handle the long tail of missions no firmware feature covers: 'if the payload temperature exceeds X, RTL', or custom gimbal choreography. The sandbox keeps scripts from breaking the flight core, which is why scripting is safe to hand to field engineers.

t: ArduPilot: Your First Mission: Auto Waypoints
title: ArduPilot: Your First Mission: Auto Waypoints
description: The hello-world: plan waypoints in Mission Planner or QGroundControl, upload, switch to Auto, watch the vehicle fly the pattern and RTL. In SITL first, always. The mission items — takeoff, waypoints, loiter, land — plus DO commands for the camera are the vocabulary. The professional step is the pre-flight: EKF happy, GPS lock, geofence set, RTL altitude above the tallest obstacle.

t: ArduPilot: Terrain Following and Precision Landing
title: ArduPilot: Terrain Following and Precision Landing
description: ArduPilot's advanced navigation: terrain following uses SRTM data or a rangefinder to hold AGL altitude over hills; precision landing fuses IR-LOCK or visual beacons to land on a target within centimeters. These are the features that turn 'a drone' into 'a tool' — repeatable, precise, boring in the best way. The tuning is in the sensor: rangefinder quality determines terrain-following quality.
key_facts: Landing offsets trended as maintenance data

title: ArduPilot: Tuning: PIDs and Filters
description: ArduPilot tuning is the craft: rate PIDs per axis, filter frequencies for gyro noise, throttle hover learning, and the AutoTune feature that flies excitation patterns and sets gains itself. The method is measure (vibration plots), filter (notch the noise), then tune (step responses). A tuned Copter holds position in wind; an untuned one wanders. The log — always the log — shows which.

t: ArduPilot: Rover and Boat: Ground and Water
title: ArduPilot: Rover and Boat: Ground and Water
description: ArduPilot is not just aircraft: Rover drives Ackermann, skid-steer, and omnidirectional ground vehicles; Boat handles water with wind-aware navigation. title: ArduPilot: Debugging: DataFlash Logs
description: ArduPilot's DataFlash logs are legendary in depth: every sensor, every EKF innovation, every controller output. The debugging ladder is vibration (mechanical health), EKF innovations (estimator health), then controller tracking. The community's log-analysis wisdom — 'check vibrations first' — has saved more aircraft than any feature. Download the log, look at the plots, believe the plots.

t: ArduPilot: Failsafes: The Layers of Safety
title: ArduPilot: Failsafes: The Layers of Safety
description: ArduPilot's failsafe layers: RC loss, GCS loss, GPS loss, battery (multiple stages), geofence, EKF failsafe — each with configured actions and the famous 'continue vs RTL vs land' decisions. The battery failsafe's staged response (warn, RTL, land) reflects hard-won field wisdom. Configuring failsafes is safety engineering with the vehicle's real performance numbers, validated in SITL with faults injected.
key_facts: Layered: RC, GCS, GPS, battery, geofence, EKF

title: ArduPilot: Companion Integration and MAVLink Routing
description: ArduPilot pairs with companions over MAVLink: vision, 4G/5G links, cloud relays. The routing (serial, UDP, CAN) is the plumbing, and the discipline is the same as PX4's — the flight core stays authoritative, companions advise. ArduPilot's MAVLink routing between multiple ground stations and vehicles is a quiet strength for fleet operations.

t: ArduPilot: Testing: SITL, HIL, and the Test Matrix
title: ArduPilot: Testing: SITL, HIL, and the Test Matrix
description: ArduPilot's testing is famously thorough: SITL for every vehicle type, autotest suites flying scripted missions in sim on every commit, HIL for hardware truth. The autotest matrix — hundreds of missions across vehicles — is the project's immune system. Contributors run the relevant slice; maintainers run it all. This is how a volunteer project out-tests many commercial ones.
